4: employer Kansas City radio station (no qualifiers). Means she was employed by a Kansas City radio station (initial job). No location qualifier but object is "Kansas City radio station". Could be ambiguous.

7: duplicate of 1 (same as id1). occupation radio personality.

9: employer KYSR Star 98.7, qualifiers location Los Angeles, duration nearly nine years, position held morning show host. So similar to 3 but expressed as employer relation with qualifiers. However relation is employer, not hosted. The assertion: Jamie White's employer is KYSR Star 98.7, with qualifiers indicating location, duration, position held. This conveys that she worked at KYSR Star 98.7 in Los Angeles for nearly nine years as morning show host. That's essentially same proposition as 3? 3 says she hosted mornings on KYSR Star 98.7, location Los Angeles, approx nearly nine years. 9 says employer KYSR Star 98.7 with qualifiers location Los Angeles, duration nearly nine years, position held morning show host. Both assert she was morning show host at KYSR Star 98.7 in Los Angeles for nearly nine years. Are they equivalent? The core proposition differs: 3 asserts she hosted mornings (a role) on that program; 9 asserts her employer is that station with qualifiers indicating she held that position. The essential proposition about her role and duration is same. The relation differs (hosted vs employer). But per rules, representation differences allowed if complete assertions remain equivalent. Here 3 includes subject, relation hosted, object program, qualifiers location and approx duration. 9 includes relation employer, object station, qualifiers location, duration, position held. Does 9 convey that she hosted mornings? Yes via qualifier position held "morning show host". That's a role. However 3 asserts she hosted mornings (the program) whereas 9 asserts she was employed by the station and held that position. Could there be a scenario where she is employed but not necessarily hosting mornings? The qualifier "position held" indicates she was morning show host, which matches. So both convey same complete proposition: Jamie White was morning show host on KYSR Star 98.7 in Los Angeles for nearly nine years. The difference in relation type may be considered equivalent because they encode same fact. According to allowed representation differences: "A descriptive qualifier is redundant only if its information is already encoded in that candidate's other fields." Here 9 uses employer relation plus qualifier position held to convey hosting. 3 uses hosted relation directly. Are they considered equivalent? I think yes, because they assert same proposition. The rule says "Synonymous entity names and predicates, abbreviations, spelling/date-format variations and correctly inverted relations." Employer vs hosted is not an inversion but a different predicate. However they both describe employment and role. Might be considered not equivalent because relation differs. Example given: "E has participant P" and "P participated in E" are inverses. Employer vs hosted is not inverse. So maybe not allowed. The core proposition differs: one says she hosted a program; the other says she was employed by station with position held. The position held qualifier adds the hosting info, but the primary relation is employer. Could the fact "Jamie White employed by KYSR Star 98.7" be true even if she didn't host mornings? Yes. The employer claim is just a way to express that. I think they are equivalent.

But need to be strict. The rule: "Allow these only when the complete assertions remain equivalent." If we can rephrase employer+position held as hosted, it's equivalent. I'd treat as duplicate.

Are they equivalent to 5? 5 says employer KYSR (present?). Could be ambiguous. Since 5 lacks qualifier, could be current or past. 17 explicitly former. Not equivalent.

payload.title: Jamie White
payload.paragraph_text: Jamie White is an American radio personality and actress who is most notable for having hosted mornings on KYSR Star 98.7 in Los Angeles for nearly nine years. Initially hired by a Kansas City radio station, she took a string of broadcasting jobs that had led to her former job at KYSR.
